items.summary: Crude oil from a grounded tanker has reached Omani mainland beaches. The sanctioned vessel, Caroline Bezengi, is leaking nearly one million barrels. Contamination has spread north of Qabiliyah Island, endangering a marine protected area. Southern coasts of Masirah Island may also be affected soon. Satellite images show the spill covers over six hundred square kilometers.

items.title: Gujarat Pipavav Port Q1 FY27 profit rises 42% to ₹148 cr
items.summary: Revenue from operations climbs 33% to ₹332 crore

items.title: Container rail movement commences between Chennai port and ICD Sanathnagar
items.summary: The inaugural movement, operated by CONCOR in association with OOCL, comprised a 40-wagon container rake with 14 FEUs and 18 TEUs, aggregating 46 TEUs

items.title: Why we should all be worried about AI in elections
items.summary: Deepfakes dominate headlines, but the real danger lies in opaque AI systems that make up election infrastructure.

items.title: JSW Neo, Bhutan's DGPC ink pact to jointly develop 920 MW Punatsangchhu-III project
items.summary: JSW Neo Energy has partnered with Bhutan's Druk Green Power Corporation to jointly develop the 920-MW Punatsangchhu-III hydroelectric project in Bhutan. This venture marks JSW Energy's first power generation project outside India.

items.title: South Western Railway begins Vande Bharat safety trials in critical Western Ghat Section
items.summary: The field trials are significant considering the ghat section between Sakleshpur and Subrahmanya Road is among the most technically demanding stretches on the Bengaluru-Mangaluru railway line

items.title: Russia’s petrol crunch sends Moscow shopping for Indian fuel
items.summary: Russia has imported petrol from India for the first time as Ukrainian attacks on its refineries deepen domestic fuel shortages. Kpler data showed the first shipment arrived on August 5, with more potentially following. Nayara Energy supplied the fuel, shipped through Russian-linked tankers via Egypt. Refinery disruptions have cut Russian processing rates, forcing Moscow to curb fuel exports.

items.title: Shipping Ministry approves Rs 334.89-cr flyover at Visakhapatnam Port to ease cargo movement
items.summary: The 3.584-km elevated corridor would separate road and rail traffic within the port

items.title: India targets 10-fold clean fuel output jump in next 5-10 years to curb imports
items.summary: India aims for a tenfold increase in compressed biogas production over the next decade. The government plans to address supply chain uncertainties and simplify business processes. Offtake assurance and stable pricing mechanisms will be implemented for producers. Financial support and credit guarantees will encourage new plant development. This initiative seeks to enhance energy security and reduce

items.title: India's power demand seen rising 6.5-7.5% this fiscal as hotter, drier weather boosts cooling needs: Crisil
items.summary: India's power demand is estimated to rise 6.5-7.5 per cent year-on-year this fiscal to 1,825-1,835 billion units (BU), driven mainly by higher cooling requirements amid expectations of higher temperatures and lower rainfall due to El Nino conditions, according to a report by Crisil Intelligence.

items.title: Centre weighs pantograph charging model for high-capacity e-buses
items.summary: Government evaluating ₹25-50 lakh pantograph chargers for 18-metre e-buses, weighing faster charging against higher infrastructure costs

items.title: Ethanol, EVs must coexist in India's clean mobility transition; E20 mileage impact limited: IFGE
items.summary: IFGE said India needs a diversified energy strategy comprising ethanol, electric vehicles, hybrids, CNG and hydrogen, particularly as nearly 300 million internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles remain on the country's roads.

items.title: OPEC oil output rises further in July led by Gulf producers, Reuters survey shows
items.summary: In July, OPEC made a remarkable recovery by increasing oil production to 19.85 million barrels per day. Gulf nations resumed supplies that were previously disrupted, while Iraq reported significant production gains. Iran also managed to increase its exports, though a U.S. blockade eventually hampered shipments. Meanwhile, Libya continued to pump oil without being affected by regional conflicts, ma

items.title: ONGC, Shell India ink pact to explore deepwater blocks, LNG sourcing
items.summary: ONGC and Shell Energy India have signed a non-binding agreement for exploration. They will explore deepwater and ultra-deepwater oil and gas opportunities together. The companies will also assess potential liquefied natural gas sourcing options. This collaboration aims to enhance India's energy security and domestic resource development. The partnership supports India's transition towards a more g

items.title: India considers curbing use of sugarcane for ethanol to tame record-high sugar market
items.summary: India may limit sugarcane use for ethanol to increase sugar production with an aim to stabilise record-high sugar prices and ensure smooth domestic supply. Reduced rainfall in key states has raised concerns about next year's sugar output. The government might allow corn and rice for ethanol to maintain its blending program.

items.title: India expands LNG sourcing from 6 to 15 countries to cut supply risks: Govt
items.summary: India has nearly trebled its liquefied natural gas suppliers to fifteen countries. The nation also broadened its crude oil sourcing network to forty-one countries. This diversification reduces dependence on any single supplier or transit route. India is also expanding its strategic petroleum storage capacity to manage supply shocks. These measures strengthen the country's energy supply resilience

items.title: India's peak power demand rises 12% in April-June, evening supply gap widens to 3,045 MW: Govt
items.summary: India's peak electricity demand rose 12 per cent from April to June over the same period last year. An all-time high of 270.8 gigawatts was recorded in May. June saw an evening supply gap of over three thousand megawatts.

items.title: AI’s volatile power demand is damaging its own data centers
items.summary: AI data centres’ volatile power demand is damaging batteries, turbines and other equipment, raising downtime costs, delaying projects and creating wider grid-stability risks.

items.title: Iran ties Hormuz reopening to US concessions on several demands
items.summary: Iran says a deal with Oman on new shipping lanes through the Strait of Hormuz is in its final stages, but reopening the strategic waterway depends on U.S. concessions, including compensation, sanctions relief and an end to military threats. The developments come amid heightened regional tensions and attacks on shipping.

items.title: Coal stocks at power plants may fall 20% by Sept-end
items.summary: Coal stocks at Indian power plants are expected to fall to 24-30 million tonnes by September-end from about 37 million tonnes currently, amid seasonal supply constraints, deficient monsoon and higher temperatures, before rebuilding from mid-November.

items.title: India achieves 300 GW renewable energy capacity, 60% of 500 GW target by 2030
items.summary: India has achieved over 300 GW of non-fossil fuel power capacity. This milestone represents more than sixty percent of the nation's 2030 goal. Solar and wind power are key contributors to this significant energy transition. Domestic manufacturing capabilities have also been strengthened for supply chain independence. This progress positions India for industrial competitiveness and energy independe

items.title: India's future nuclear fleet may need 5,400 tonnes uranium annually; domestic supply meets about 30%: Parliamentary panel
items.summary: India’s nuclear expansion could sharply raise uranium demand, with PHWRs alone expected to require around 5,400 tonnes of uranium oxide annually. A Parliamentary Committee flagged that domestic production currently meets only 30% of this requirement and urged faster mining, strategic stockpiles, overseas sourcing and clearer timelines to secure long-term fuel supplies.

items.title: US Senate Russia sanctions vote raises risk for Indian crude supplies, says Kpler
items.summary: A US Senate vote advances tougher sanctions on Russia, potentially disrupting crude oil supplies. However, immediate impacts on India and China's oil flows are unlikely. India's reliance on Russian crude has significantly increased since 2022. Replacing these supplies quickly would be difficult and could tighten global markets. This situation raises concerns for India's energy security and import

items.title: India Energy Week moves to Kolkata, to be held from January 28-31 next year
items.summary: India Energy Week 2027 will be held in Kolkata from January 28-31, marking a shift from Goa, where a Rs 1,000-crore convention centre was built as a permanent venue. The fifth edition will take place at the Biswa Bangla Convention Centre in New Town, with preparations reviewed by Oil Minister Hardeep Singh Puri.

items.title: GOBARdhan Scheme can help reduce gas imports by $5 billion, says IBA
items.summary: The GOBARdhan Scheme is expected to significantly reduce India's gas import bill. This initiative aims to convert organic waste into clean energy sources. The scheme will also decrease fertilizer imports and subsidy burdens for the nation. It is projected to create numerous employment opportunities in rural areas.

items.title: India’s $40 billion Russian oil lifeline shouldn’t buckle under Trump’s 100% tariff threat: GTRI
items.summary: As long as it proves to be economically feasible, India should persist in acquiring Russian crude oil. A new Senate bill from the US threatens to impose significant tariffs on countries engaging in Russian energy purchases. Being one of the leading buyers, India might suffer trade penalties. This leads to a critical choice between accessing cheaper oil and retaining US export possibilities.

items.title: India has built energy resilience to withstand external shocks, says Puri
items.summary: India has enhanced its energy security by diversifying crude oil supplies. Strategic infrastructure expansion and domestic exploration investments are key initiatives. The nation is better prepared for geopolitical disruptions than ever before. New schemes aim to accelerate deepwater oil and gas exploration efforts. India's growing energy demand will significantly drive global oil consumption.

items.title: L&T bags major offshore orders worth Rs 5,000-10,000 crore from ONGC for pipeline replacement
items.summary: Larsen & Toubro has secured significant offshore orders from ONGC. These orders are valued between five thousand and ten thousand crore rupees. The projects involve pipeline replacement and well head platforms off India's west coast. L&T Energy Hydrocarbon Offshore will execute these critical engineering projects. This reaffirms L&T's role in developing India's energy infrastructure.

items.title: India cuts energy import dependence to 42%, oil imports still meet 90% of demand: CII-EY
items.summary: India's primary energy import dependence has decreased to forty-two percent by FY25. Crude oil imports still meet nearly ninety percent of domestic demand. Natural gas import dependence has increased to about fifty percent. Coal import dependence has fallen to around eighteen percent due to production. Energy security requires clean energy and domestic production for resilience.

items.title: India may charge gas users to fund planned $42 billion fuel reserves, sources say
items.summary: India is considering levies on cooking gas and natural gas consumers to fund a proposed $42 billion multi-fuel strategic reserve programme aimed at strengthening energy security after supply disruptions during the Iran conflict. The plan would expand strategic reserves beyond crude oil to include LNG and LPG storage for the first time.

items.title: Indian refiners buy Middle East and West African crude, sources say
items.summary: Indian refiners have stepped up crude oil purchases, with Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals buying 1 million barrels of Oman crude through a tender, according to trade sources. The cargo was purchased at a premium of about $3 a barrel over dated Brent, with Mitsui & Co Energy Trading Singapore identified as the seller.

items.title: Adani Green to seek board nod to raise up to $1 billion
items.summary: Adani Green Energy is set to seek board approval to raise Rs 6,150 crore ($750 million) to Rs 8,200 crore ($1 billion) through the qualified institutional placement (QIP) route, said people aware of the matter.Two group companies had got approval of their boards for fundraising on May 13 —Adani Enterprises (Rs 12,500 crore) and Adani Transmission (Rs 8,500 crore).The exercise is part of a group pl

items.title: Office realty leasing rises 30%, on track to beat last year high
items.summary: Mumbai: Robust demand for office spaces has pushed commercial property leasing in the first three quarters of 2019 by 30% from a year ago, taking it closer to entire 2018’s performance and making sure that this year surpasses the peak touched last year.Driven by tech corporates — accounting for about a third of the leasing activity — office space take-up touched 47 million sq ft in the first nine
